column1: Design a partial-order-broadcast protocol for a collaborative editing backend that only needs causal delivery ordering, and explain why it can avoid the overhead of full total-order broadcast.
Design a tiered storage migration policy that moves cold shards from SSD to object storage without violating a service's read-latency SLA for rarely accessed keys.
Design a distributed leader-election protocol that must remain correct when the cluster spans two network fabrics with asymmetric partition probabilities.
Design a request-hedging strategy for a fan-out read path that reduces tail latency without multiplying backend load beyond a bounded factor.
Design a schema-registry-backed message format evolution strategy for a streaming pipeline that guarantees old consumers never receive an unparseable payload.
Design a distributed rate limiter that must enforce a global quota shared across regions with sub-100ms propagation of quota consumption.
Design a replicated write-ahead log service supporting multiple independent tenants with per-tenant durability tuning without cross-tenant interference in fsync latency.
Design a cluster-wide admission-control system that sheds load fairly across tenants during an overload event using a token-bucket hierarchy.
Design a cross-shard secondary-index maintenance protocol that stays consistent with the primary data despite independent shard failures.
Design a multi-region conflict-free replicated queue that preserves per-key FIFO ordering while allowing concurrent regional writers.
Design a hierarchical failure-detection protocol for a 100,000-node cluster that bounds false-positive suspicion rate without a fully connected heartbeat mesh.
Prove that a specific epidemic-style anti-entropy protocol converges within O(log n) rounds with high probability, given a bounded node degree.
Design a formally specified reconfigurable-quorum protocol and prove it prevents overlapping quorums from diverging during a live membership change.
Design a globally consistent snapshot-isolation protocol across independently-sharded storage engines and prove it satisfies snapshot-read atomicity without global locks.
Design a provably optimal replica-placement algorithm minimizing worst-case cross-region latency subject to a fault-tolerance constraint, and prove its approximation ratio.
Design a formally verified state-transfer protocol for reconfiguring a Byzantine quorum system and prove it preserves safety across arbitrarily many overlapping reconfigurations.
Design a data structure supporting persistent (multi-version) range-sum queries under both point updates and full-array historical rollbacks in sublinear time per operation.
Design an algorithm for maintaining an approximate top-k frequent-items sketch under a stream with deletions, and derive its error bound as a function of sketch width.
Design an exact algorithm for computing the Steiner tree in a graph with a small number of terminal nodes, and analyze its exponential dependence on terminal count.
Design a fractional-cascading-based data structure for answering iterated dominance queries across multiple sorted lists in O(log n) per query after preprocessing.
Design an online algorithm for interval scheduling with cancellation penalties and derive its competitive ratio against an optimal offline scheduler.
Design a randomized incremental algorithm for computing a Delaunay triangulation and derive its expected O(n log n) runtime via backward analysis.
Design a heavy-path decomposition of a tree to support path-update and path-query operations in O(log^2 n), and explain the role of segment trees over each chain.
Design an approximation algorithm for the metric k-center problem with a provable 2-approximation guarantee, and prove the guarantee is tight.
Design a data structure for dynamic planar point location supporting insertions and deletions of line segments in polylogarithmic time per operation.
Design an algorithm for computing a minimum-weight perfect matching in a general graph in polynomial time, outlining the primal-dual structure of Edmonds' blossom algorithm at a high level.
Design a parameterized algorithm for the vertex cover problem with a running time of O(2^k * n) and prove the kernelization bound that makes this tractable for small k.
Design a fully persistent hash-array-mapped trie supporting O(log n) structural sharing per update, and analyze the amortized cost of path copying.
Design a randomized algorithm for finding a global minimum cut in a hypergraph and derive its success probability per trial.
Prove a tight lower bound on the cell-probe complexity of the predecessor-search problem, connecting it to the fusion-tree upper bound.
Design a parallel algorithm for computing biconnected components with O(log n) depth and prove its work-efficiency.
Prove matching upper and lower bounds on the space complexity of an exact distinct-elements-counting streaming algorithm, contrasting with the approximate HyperLogLog bound.
Design a succinct representation of a planar graph supporting O(1) adjacency queries in information-theoretically optimal space, and prove the space bound is tight.
Design an architecture for a real-time collaborative CAD tool that must merge concurrent geometric edits from multiple engineers without producing an invalid mesh.
Design an architecture for a global rate-limited SMS delivery platform that must respect per-carrier throughput agreements across dozens of countries.
Design an architecture for a personalization engine that must serve cold-start users with a fallback model while a per-user model warms up online.
Design an architecture for a distributed build system that caches compilation artifacts across a large engineering org while guaranteeing cache correctness under non-deterministic compiler flags.
Design an architecture for a multi-region secrets-rotation pipeline that must never leave a service temporarily unable to decrypt with any valid key version.
Design an architecture for a real-time bidding platform's budget-pacing system that prevents overspend across thousands of concurrent auctions per advertiser.
Design an architecture for a genomic-data processing pipeline that must reproducibly reprocess petabyte-scale datasets when an upstream reference database is updated.
Design an architecture for a distributed feature-engineering platform that guarantees point-in-time correctness for backtesting without leaking future information into historical feature values.
Design an architecture for a large-scale document-similarity search system that must support both approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and exact deduplication at ingestion time.
Design an architecture for a multi-tenant workflow-orchestration platform (Airflow-style) that isolates a runaway tenant's DAG from starving other tenants' scheduled jobs.
Design the end-to-end architecture for a national-scale digital-identity verification system with strict availability and auditability guarantees under adversarial load.
Design the architecture for a real-time market-surveillance system that must detect cross-venue manipulation patterns within a regulatory-mandated latency window.
Design a globally fault-tolerant architecture for a satellite ground-station command-and-control system where a dropped command can have physical consequences.
Design a quantum circuit implementing Grover's algorithm for unstructured search and derive the optimal number of oracle iterations to maximize success probability.
Explain how the quantum phase estimation algorithm extracts an eigenvalue's phase to precision 2^-n using n ancilla qubits, and derive the circuit's success probability.
Design a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz for finding a molecule's ground-state energy, and explain the barren-plateau problem's effect on gradient-based optimization.
Explain how the quantum Fourier transform circuit achieves O(n^2) gate complexity versus the classical FFT's O(n log n), and why this asymmetry still yields exponential speedup for period-finding.
Design a quantum error-correcting code (e.g. the 5-qubit code) and prove it satisfies the quantum error-correction conditions (Knill-Laflamme) for arbitrary single-qubit errors.

Explain how the HHL algorithm solves a linear system exponentially faster than classical methods under specific sparsity and conditioning assumptions, and identify what makes reading out the full solution vector intractable.
Design a surface-code-based fault-tolerant quantum computing architecture and derive how the code distance must scale with physical error rate to achieve a target logical error rate.
Explain how quantum amplitude estimation achieves a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo sampling, and derive its query complexity as a function of target precision.
Design a quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) circuit for MaxCut and analyze how circuit depth trades off against approximation ratio.

Explain how the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm's oracle structure guarantees deterministic distinguishing of constant versus balanced functions, and why this doesn't translate into practically useful speedup.
Design a quantum walk-based search algorithm on a graph and derive its hitting-time speedup over the corresponding classical random walk.
Design a measurement-based quantum computing scheme using a cluster state and explain how adaptive single-qubit measurements implement universal computation.
Prove the no-cloning theorem from the linearity of quantum mechanics and explain its role in guaranteeing the security of quantum key distribution.
Design Shor's algorithm's modular-exponentiation circuit and derive its qubit and gate-count requirements as a function of the number being factored.
Prove a tight lower bound on the query complexity of Grover's search algorithm, showing quadratic speedup is optimal for unstructured search.
Design a topological quantum computing scheme based on non-abelian anyons and explain how braiding operations achieve fault-tolerant gates without active error correction.
Prove the threshold theorem for fault-tolerant quantum computation, showing that arbitrarily long quantum computations are possible below a critical physical error rate.
Design an XLA-style operator-fusion pass that merges elementwise and reduction operations into a single kernel, and derive the memory-bandwidth savings versus unfused execution.
Explain how a Triton kernel's block-level tiling abstraction maps to underlying GPU thread-block and shared-memory resources, and design a tiling scheme for a fused softmax kernel.
Design a layout-assignment pass for a tensor compiler that chooses between row-major and tiled memory layouts based on downstream operator access patterns.
Explain how an ML compiler's auto-scheduling search (e.g. Halide/TVM-style) explores a loop-transformation space, and design a cost model to prune it effectively.
Design a compiler pass that rewrites a dynamic-shape computation graph into a small set of shape-specialized kernels while bounding recompilation overhead.
Explain how XLA's while-loop lowering handles a data-dependent iteration count on a fixed-topology accelerator, and design the buffer-donation strategy needed to avoid excess memory allocation.

Design a memory-planning pass for an ML compiler that reuses buffers across a computation graph's lifetime to minimize peak accelerator memory, and formalize the interference-graph coloring problem it solves.
Explain how a Triton compiler lowers a high-level block-pointer abstraction down to a target-specific instruction schedule, and identify where auto-tuning is required versus static scheduling.
Design an ML compiler's automatic differentiation pass operating directly on a graph IR, and explain how it must handle control-flow constructs (loops, conditionals) to remain correct.
Design a compiler-level quantization pass that inserts fake-quantization nodes for quantization-aware training, and analyze how it must preserve gradient flow through non-differentiable rounding.
Explain how a polyhedral compilation framework represents nested-loop iteration spaces for an ML kernel, and design an affine scheduling transformation that improves data locality.

Design a cross-accelerator lowering pipeline that compiles a single high-level ML graph to both a GPU (Triton/CUDA) and a custom ASIC backend, and identify which optimization passes must be backend-specific versus shared.
Design a formally specified buffer-aliasing analysis for an ML compiler's in-place-update optimization and prove it never introduces a data race between overlapping operations.

Design an auto-tuning search space and cost model for a Triton kernel's tile-size and pipelining-stage parameters, and prove the search converges to a near-optimal configuration under a bounded compile-time budget.

Design a compiler pass that automatically inserts activation-recomputation checkpoints in a computation graph to satisfy a hard memory budget while minimizing added recompute FLOPs, and formalize it as an optimization problem.

Design a formally verified graph-rewriting system for an ML compiler that proves every optimization pass preserves the numerical semantics of the original computation up to a bounded floating-point error.

Design a compiler infrastructure that automatically partitions and schedules a large computation graph across a heterogeneous accelerator mesh (different chip generations), proving the resulting schedule respects all data dependencies and memory constraints.
Design a happens-before-based data-race detector for a concurrent program and prove it never reports a false positive under the vector-clock algorithm it uses.
Formalize the proof that a lock-free stack implementation is linearizable by identifying its linearization points for push and pop operations.
Design a rely-guarantee proof methodology for verifying a concurrent program's invariant, and explain how the rely and guarantee conditions decouple reasoning about interfering threads.
Formalize a proof that a specific readers-writer lock implementation is deadlock-free using a resource-ordering argument.
Design a session-type-based verification approach for a message-passing concurrent program and prove it guarantees the absence of a specific communication mismatch.
Formalize the proof of linearizability for a lock-free queue using a simulation argument to an atomic reference implementation.
Design a separation-logic-based proof of memory safety for a concurrent program using fine-grained locking, and explain the role of the lock invariant in the proof.
Formalize a proof that a specific concurrent garbage collector never reclaims a reachable object, using an invariant over the mark-and-sweep phases interleaved with mutator threads.
Design a model-checking approach for verifying mutual exclusion in a concurrent program with an unbounded number of processes, using a parameterized-verification cutoff argument.
Design a formal proof using concurrent separation logic that a specific fine-grained concurrent hash table implementation has no data races on bucket resizing.
Formalize the proof of deadlock-freedom for a concurrent program using a wait-for-graph acyclicity invariant maintained across all reachable states.
Design a compositional verification framework for a concurrent program built from verified components, and explain what interface contracts must hold for the composition to preserve safety.
Design a machine-checked linearizability proof for a wait-free multi-producer multi-consumer queue in a proof assistant, specifying the abstraction relation used.
Formalize and prove progress (lock-freedom) for a specific non-blocking algorithm using an amortized potential-function argument encoded in a proof assistant.
Design a formally verified proof that a specific weak-memory-model relaxation (e.g. under RC11) still permits a given concurrent algorithm to satisfy its intended correctness property.

Design a fully machine-checked proof of linearizability and lock-freedom for a concurrent skip list, formalized in a dependently typed proof assistant, including the auxiliary-state simulation argument.

Formalize and prove correctness of a distributed consensus protocol's implementation (not just its abstract algorithm) down to the level of its message-passing code, using a refinement-based verification framework.
Explain how the Laplace mechanism achieves epsilon-differential privacy for a numeric query, and derive the noise scale required as a function of the query's sensitivity.
Design a differentially private histogram-release mechanism and derive its accuracy guarantee as a function of epsilon and the number of bins.
Explain how the exponential mechanism achieves differential privacy for non-numeric query outputs, and derive its utility guarantee in terms of the quality-score sensitivity.
Design a differentially private stochastic gradient descent algorithm (DP-SGD) and explain the role of per-example gradient clipping in bounding sensitivity.
Explain how the sparse vector technique answers many threshold queries under a bounded total privacy budget, and derive why naive composition would exhaust the budget faster.
Design a locally differentially private data-collection protocol (e.g. randomized response) and derive its privacy-utility trade-off as a function of the randomization probability.
Prove the basic composition theorem for differential privacy and derive the tighter bound achieved by the advanced composition theorem using concentration inequalities.

Design a differentially private federated learning protocol combining DP-SGD with secure aggregation, and analyze how the privacy accounting must account for both client-level and record-level privacy.
Explain how Renyi differential privacy provides tighter composition bounds than standard (epsilon, delta)-DP, and derive the conversion formula between the two definitions.
Design a differentially private synthetic-data-generation algorithm and derive the trade-off between the fidelity of downstream statistics and the privacy budget consumed.
Design a private PAC learning algorithm and derive how the sample complexity must scale with the privacy parameter to preserve the same learnability guarantee as the non-private setting.
Explain how the Gaussian mechanism's privacy guarantee under zero-concentrated differential privacy composes more tightly than under standard DP, and derive the noise-scale formula.
Prove a tight lower bound on the sample complexity required to answer a set of linear queries under differential privacy, using a reconstruction-attack argument.
Design a differentially private algorithm for releasing a graph's degree distribution and prove its accuracy guarantee under edge-level privacy.
Prove the optimality of the Gaussian mechanism among all noise-adding mechanisms achieving a given zero-concentrated differential privacy guarantee, under an L2-sensitivity constraint.
Design a differentially private algorithm achieving the optimal sample complexity for private mean estimation under a heavy-tailed distribution, and prove a matching lower bound.
Prove a tight trade-off between accuracy and privacy for answering a large class of statistical queries simultaneously, using a fingerprinting-code-based lower-bound argument.
Prove that a one-time pad achieves perfect (information-theoretic) secrecy using Shannon's definition, and explain why key reuse breaks this guarantee.
Derive the wiretap channel's secrecy capacity and explain how it bounds the maximum rate of information-theoretically secure communication given a degraded eavesdropper channel.
Prove that a secret-sharing scheme with a threshold of t out of n parties is information-theoretically secure against any coalition of fewer than t parties.
Explain how privacy amplification via a randomness extractor converts a weakly random source and a short shared secret into a longer information-theoretically secure key.
Derive the min-entropy requirement for a source to be safely used in a leftover-hash-lemma-based key-derivation function with information-theoretic security.
Prove the security of a quantum-key-distribution protocol (BB84) against an unbounded eavesdropper, using the uncertainty principle to bound information gain versus disturbance.

Design an information-theoretically secure multi-party computation protocol for computing a sum over private inputs, using additive secret sharing, and prove its security against a semi-honest adversary.

Derive the information-theoretic bound on the number of queries an adversary needs to fully reconstruct a database from noisy aggregate statistics, connecting it to the differential-privacy reconstruction-attack literature.
Prove that a specific authentication code (MAC) construction achieves information-theoretic unforgeability against a computationally unbounded adversary, given a bound on key reuse.
Explain how network coding can achieve information-theoretically secure communication against a wiretapper who observes a bounded subset of links, and derive the achievable secrecy rate.
Derive the information-theoretic capacity region for a broadcast channel with confidential messages, and explain what it implies about the fundamental limit of physical-layer security.
Design an information-theoretically secure oblivious transfer protocol using a noisy channel as a resource, and prove its security against a computationally unbounded receiver.
Prove a tight information-theoretic lower bound on the communication complexity required for two parties to compute a specific function while leaking no information beyond the output.
Derive the secrecy capacity of a Gaussian wiretap channel and prove the achievability using a random-binning coding argument.
Prove the impossibility of unconditionally secure bit commitment using only classical channels, and contrast this with the security achievable using quantum channels under specific assumptions.
Prove a tight bound on the information-theoretic secret-key capacity of a source-model key-agreement protocol given correlated randomness observed by two parties and an eavesdropper.
Derive the exact information-theoretic trade-off between secrecy rate and storage rate in a biometric secret-binding system, and prove the achievability of the resulting rate region.
Design a secure firmware attestation chain that binds a device's measured boot sequence to a hardware-rooted key, and identify the trust assumptions about the root of trust.
Explain how a threshold ECDSA signing protocol distributes the signing key across parties without ever reconstructing it, and identify what makes the nonce generation step security-critical.
Design a certificate-pinning strategy for a mobile app that avoids breaking connectivity during a legitimate CA key rotation.
Design a secure multi-tenant key-management service that isolates tenant keys such that a compromised tenant's IAM policy cannot expose another tenant's key material.

Explain how a padding-oracle-resistant authenticated encryption mode (e.g. AES-GCM) prevents the classical CBC padding-oracle attack, and identify what new failure mode nonce reuse introduces instead.
Design a hardware security module failover protocol that maintains signing availability during a primary HSM outage without ever exposing key material outside the HSM boundary.

Explain how a threshold BLS signature aggregation scheme enables a validator committee to jointly sign without a designated leader, and prove its unforgeability against a bounded-corruption adversary.
Design a secure protocol for rotating an encryption-at-rest key across a live production database without a maintenance window, ensuring no data is ever unencrypted-at-rest during the transition.
Design a formally specified proof that a specific PKI certificate-validation implementation correctly rejects all malformed certificate chains, including a name-constraint bypass class of attacks.

Design an attestation-based confidential-computing pipeline spanning multiple untrusted cloud providers, and prove the end-to-end data-confidentiality guarantee holds even if any single provider is compromised.
Design a query-optimizer statistics-collection subsystem that estimates join selectivity under correlated columns without exponential sampling cost, and analyze the estimation-error trade-off.
Explain how a database's multi-version storage engine determines the garbage-collection horizon for old row versions in the presence of long-running analytical queries.
Design a distributed SQL engine's distributed deadlock-free two-phase locking protocol across independently-owned shard leaders.
Design a columnar database's late-materialization strategy for filter-then-project query plans, and analyze when it outperforms early materialization.
Explain how a database's adaptive radix tree index balances memory efficiency against lookup speed compared to a traditional B+ tree for in-memory workloads.
Design a database checkpoint mechanism using fuzzy checkpointing that avoids pausing transaction processing, and explain how recovery reconciles the resulting inconsistent checkpoint image.
Design a query-compilation strategy (JIT-compiled query plans) for an analytical database and analyze the compilation-overhead versus execution-speed trade-off for short-lived queries.
Design a distributed database's global secondary-index consistency protocol that tolerates the base-table shard and the index shard failing independently.

Explain how a database's cost-based optimizer estimates cardinality for a multi-way join using histogram-based statistics, and design a correction for the independence-assumption's systematic underestimation.
Design a hybrid transactional-analytical processing (HTAP) system's dual-storage-format synchronization mechanism that keeps a row-store and column-store consistent under high write throughput.
Design a distributed database's global clock-free causal-consistency protocol and prove it provides stronger guarantees than eventual consistency without requiring synchronized clocks.
Design a real-time operating system's memory-protection unit configuration that isolates safety-critical tasks from best-effort tasks without a full MMU-based virtual memory system.
Explain how a lock-free multi-producer single-consumer ring buffer avoids the ABA problem without using double-width compare-and-swap.
Design a user-space threading library's cooperative scheduler that must remain fair under a workload mixing CPU-bound and I/O-bound green threads.
Design a formally specified proof of mutual exclusion for a ticket-lock implementation under a relaxed memory model, identifying the required memory barriers.
Explain how a real-time scheduler's rate-monotonic analysis bounds worst-case response time for a set of periodic tasks, and derive the utilization bound for exact schedulability.
Design a NUMA-aware lock implementation that reduces remote-cache-line traffic under high contention compared to a standard ticket lock.
Design a formally verified real-time scheduler's admission-control test that guarantees no task set accepted can miss a deadline under worst-case execution time bounds.

Design a statistical arbitrage strategy that hedges factor exposures using a rolling PCA decomposition of the covariance matrix, and derive how estimation noise in the eigenvectors affects hedge-ratio stability.
Design an options market-making inventory model that adjusts quotes based on realized-versus-implied volatility divergence, and derive the resulting skew adjustment.
Design a cross-currency basis-swap valuation model and derive the no-arbitrage relationship it must satisfy relative to the covered interest-rate parity condition.
Design a tail-risk hedging overlay for an equity portfolio using out-of-the-money put spreads, and derive the cost-efficiency trade-off versus a simple protective put.
Design an optimal-stopping model for deciding when to exercise a callable bond, and derive the exercise boundary using a dynamic-programming formulation.
Design a bandwidth-aware chunked file-transfer protocol for a distributed backup service that adapts chunk size to observed network jitter without renegotiating the connection.
Design a distributed presence-tracking system for a messaging app that reconciles conflicting online/offline signals arriving out of order from different edge servers.
Design a quota-enforcement system for a shared multi-tenant object store that must reclaim over-quota usage gracefully without deleting a tenant's most recently written objects first.
Design an incremental-computation framework (Bloom/differential-dataflow style) for maintaining a materialized view under continuous upstream updates without full recomputation.
Design a leader-standby failover protocol for a stateful service where the standby must replay a write-ahead log before accepting traffic, and bound the resulting failover downtime.
Design an algorithm for maintaining a dynamic topological order of a DAG under edge insertions in amortized sublinear time per update.
Design a data structure for answering k-nearest-neighbor queries in a dynamic point set under a Euclidean metric with polylogarithmic update time.
Design an algorithm for computing the maximum weight independent set in an interval graph in polynomial time, and prove why this tractability doesn't extend to general graphs.
Design an architecture for a real-time translation service that must maintain per-speaker context across a multi-hour conversation while bounding memory growth.

Design an architecture for a compliance-archiving system that must make records immutable and tamper-evident while still supporting legal-hold-based selective retention beyond the default deletion policy.
Design a quantum circuit for implementing the quantum counting algorithm by combining amplitude estimation with Grover iterations, and derive its estimation-error scaling with circuit depth.
Explain how a quantum error-correcting stabilizer code's syndrome measurement circuit detects errors without collapsing the encoded logical state, and describe the role of ancilla qubits.
Design a variational quantum classifier's data-encoding circuit (angle encoding) and explain how the choice of encoding affects the expressibility of the resulting quantum kernel.

Design a Triton kernel autotuner's configuration space for a matrix-multiplication kernel and explain which parameters (block size, number of warps, pipelining stage count) most affect achieved throughput.
Design an ML compiler's constant-folding pass operating on a static computation graph and explain what invariants it must preserve when the graph contains a data-dependent control-flow node.
Explain how an ML accelerator compiler's operator-scheduling pass orders independent kernels to maximize overlap between compute and data-movement engines.
Design a happens-before-based verification approach for detecting atomicity violations (not just data races) in a concurrent program, and explain how it differs from a plain race detector.
Formalize the proof that a specific concurrent bounded buffer implementation never permits the consumer to read a slot the producer hasn't finished writing, using an invariant over buffer indices.
Design a differentially private top-k selection algorithm and derive its accuracy guarantee as a function of the privacy budget and the gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th true counts.
Explain how the moments accountant technique tracks cumulative privacy loss more tightly than basic composition for iterative algorithms like DP-SGD.
Prove that a specific two-party key-agreement protocol built from a noisy correlated-randomness source achieves a positive information-theoretically secure key rate.

Explain how a physically unclonable function (PUF) provides a hardware root of trust, and identify what statistical properties its challenge-response behavior must satisfy for information-theoretic unpredictability guarantees.
Design a hierarchical scheduler for a mixed-criticality real-time system that must guarantee high-criticality task deadlines even if low-criticality tasks are starved during an overload mode switch.
Design a multi-region database migration strategy that moves a live, high-throughput table between storage engines with zero downtime and a bounded dual-write consistency window.
Design a formally specified proof that a specific distributed rate-limiter implementation never permits more than a bounded overshoot of the configured quota under any message-delivery interleaving.
Design an approximate algorithm for the graph-coloring problem on a bounded-degree graph and derive a provable bound on the number of colors used relative to the chromatic number.

Design an architecture for a real-time credit-underwriting pipeline that combines a low-latency rules engine with an asynchronous ML risk model without blocking approval decisions on the slower model.
Design a quantum-circuit compilation pass that maps a logical circuit onto a hardware's limited qubit-connectivity graph, and derive the SWAP-gate overhead this introduces.
Design an ML compiler's automatic operator-placement pass for a heterogeneous CPU-GPU pipeline, and formalize the cost model it uses to decide which operators run on which device.
Design a formally specified proof that a specific fine-grained lock-based B-tree implementation preserves the B-tree balance invariant under concurrent insertions and deletions.
Prove a tight bound on the number of ancilla qubits required to implement a specific multi-controlled quantum gate using only single- and two-qubit gates.
Design a formally verified proof of linearizability for a persistent (non-volatile-memory) lock-free data structure that must also recover correctly after a crash mid-operation.
Prove a tight information-theoretic bound on the minimum key length required for perfectly secure computation of a specific two-party function in the information-theoretic MPC model.
Design a formally verified quantum-error-correction decoder and prove its logical error rate matches the theoretical threshold-theorem prediction for a given physical error rate.

Design a compiler-level proof that a specific ML-accelerator instruction-scheduling pass never reorders two operations with a true data dependency, formalized as a dependency-preserving simulation relation.
Prove a matching upper and lower bound on the differential-privacy sample complexity of releasing a covariance matrix under a bounded operator-norm accuracy requirement.
